scientific_goal: Determine whether a converged one-step TCN15 can be calibrated by low-variance, frequently evaluated joint energy-score updates, introduced first at short horizons and then at horizons 20 and 50, while preserving rollout stability and one-step fit.
scientific_constraints: Use validation repetitions 13 and 14 for every adaptive decision. Keep test repetitions 15 and 16 locked.

Preserve the restoring-only damped-residual TCN15 architecture, rank 20, full constant diffusion, stored 50 Hz high-pass spatial mean, native-lag velocity state, 5 percent trim, seed 0, kernel 3, channels 64 and dilations 1,2,4. Do not change architecture, diffusion family, trimming or add moment penalties.

The initial model is a fresh one-step-only TCN15 trained for eight epochs. Select its best checkpoint by validation NLL. If the final validation NLL is still improving materially, permit at most one low-learning-rate one-step continuation before score calibration.

Energy-score stages start only from a screened one-step parent. Use the existing Euclidean joint displacement-velocity energy score with position/velocity weights 2/1. Do not add a capillary-energy metric.

Reduce estimator noise by scoring 10 percent of whole batches and using eight particles at every horizon. The inverse-probability selected coefficient is therefore weight divided by 0.1. Do not return to fraction 0.005 or use a selected coefficient above 3.

Introduce score horizons as a curriculum. First use horizons 2,4,10 with normalized weights 0.2,0.3,0.5. Only after a stable short-horizon candidate should a continuation use horizons 10,20,50 with weights 0.1,0.35,0.55. Do not train horizons 20 or 50 from random initialization.

Every score fine-tune is one epoch at learning rate 3e-5 or 1e-5 so its saved checkpoint cannot hide a worsening long-horizon score behind an NLL-dominated multi-epoch selection. Start score weight at 0.03; raise only to 0.1 and then at most 0.3 if the matched lower-weight stage is stable but its expected gradient is still too weak.
Use same-parent no-score one-epoch continuations as controls before attributing rollout improvement to either the short or long score stage. Ordinary continuation is a competing explanation.

The frozen gradient diagnostic always evaluates the same audit objective: horizons 2,4,10,20,50, weights 0.1,0.1,0.15,0.25,0.4, joint weights 2/1, M8, fraction 0.1 and total coefficient 0.03. It reports each horizon separately. This audit objective may differ from the objective used to train a stage.

Require the actual validation energy-score terms emphasized by a training stage to improve within that one epoch. Inspect per-horizon gradient norms and cosines: distinguish weak long-horizon gradients, conflict with NLL, and conflict among horizons. Frozen gradients describe local directions and do not alone establish rollout improvement.

Screen every candidate on the same 32 validation paths for 5000 steps. Compare checkpoint-trimmed deformation energy, covariance, POD mean, leading modal RMS, spatial mean, PSD, survival, one-step NLL and innovation diagnostics separately. Promote at most one credible candidate to 50000 steps.

At most eight training jobs are allowed. Stop rather than adding moments, bounded diffusion, orthogonality, history noise, a new metric or a new architecture. A failed scientific hypothesis is an acceptable outcome.
advisor_guidance: Follow a staged matched study. After the fresh one-step baseline, first decide whether one low-rate one-step convergence continuation is required from its NLL history. Establish a same-parent one-step continuation control and a short-score arm from the selected one-step parent. The short arm must use horizons 2,4,10, weights 0.2,0.3,0.5, M8, fraction 0.1, coefficient 0.03, one epoch, and the same learning rate as its control. If the short arm is stable and improves its emphasized validation scores beyond the control, use it as the parent for a matched long-stage pair: a no-change short-score continuation control and a long-score continuation with horizons 10,20,50 and weights 0.1,0.35,0.55. Interpret the fixed five-horizon gradient audit together with the actual training metrics. Raise the score coefficient to 0.1 only if the long-stage terms fail to improve and the audit shows finite, directionally useful but weak expected long-horizon gradients; use 0.3 only after a stable 0.1 result remains clearly underpowered. Never change batch fraction and weight in the same comparison. Do not use weight 0.3 if it makes the selected coefficient exceed 3 or if the preceding stage harms stability. Treat a validation h20 or h50 score increase as failure of that calibration step even when NLL improves. Use change families one_step_convergence, score_control, short_score, long_score_control, long_score, and score_weight_calibration. Name the exact parent and give numerical evidence. Do not request a new loss or architecture in this study. Promote only after all useful matched comparisons are complete.

seed_runs.hypothesis: Prior TCN15 joint-score h20 reference trained from initialization with sparse score batches.
Prior h50 TCN15 reference with excellent total covariance but poor physical energy and mean.

initial_trials.hypothesis: A one-step-only TCN15 parent trained to validation-NLL convergence provides a stable initialization from which dense score updates can be interpreted.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Finite 5000-step rollouts and a flattening validation NLL history. The fixed five-horizon audit should quantify the available h20/h50 gradients before any score update.
